findings.title: canManage() checks VIEW scope, so view-only admins are treated as managers
findings.body: canManage() falls back to hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). A caller with only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource therefore passes canManage(). That grants group creation (GroupsResource.requireManage()) and any other check that relies on canManage(). Only MANAGE should be accepted here. Likely a copy-paste from canView(). The interface javadoc says 'VIEW or MANAGE groups' for canManage(), so the doc has the same mistake.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes a resource ID to hasPermission, which looks up by name
findings.body: hasPermission(groupId, ...) calls resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). Here the code passes groupResource.getId(), which is the resource's internal UUID, not its name (the group id). The lookup returns null and falls back to the all-groups resource, so the result is wrong. The same ID is then added to the granted set. The set should hold group ids, i.e. the resource names. As written, per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants are mishandled when the user search is filtered by group.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the all-groups resource is missing
findings.body: getResourceTypeResource can return null, for example when the schema is not supported or the resource is absent. policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and resource.getScopes() are then called without a null check. This will throw NPE instead of returning false.

findings.title: canViewMembers/getGroupIds use users().canView() but not the group-specific permission path correctly
findings.body: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission the early return relies on root.users().canView(). When users().canView() is false the method iterates every Groups resource and evaluates permissions per resource. The all-groups type resource itself is also of type Groups, so it is included in the iteration. Its id is added to the result as if it were a group id.

findings.title: canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership now accept group-level MANAGE_MEMBERS
findings.body: canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership now return true via canManageByGroup(user), which means MANAGE_MEMBERS on any group the user belongs to. Previously these checks required MAP_ROLES or MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP on the user. This is a deliberate-looking widening of privilege, and no test covers it.
